I use the word “pretending” in substitute for “forger,” which is what a pseudepigrapher is, so B.
Ehrman, as noted in M. Kruger, “The Authenticity of 2 Peter,”
71 (648). Ehrman states “‘Indeed, despite its common occurrence, forgery was almost
universally condemned by ancient authors.’” It may be said, then, that forgery was condemned in
the early centuries and perhaps can be class
ified as a form of lying.
